title: Isomorphism reindexing normalizes adic realization comparisons
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], for each finite $E\subset\Omega$ put $B_{E,T}=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_T$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], $E_T=B_{E,T}[1/\varpi_E]$, and $R_T=p_T^*\underline\Omega$, where $\underline\Omega(S)$ consists of continuous functions on a profinite set $S$ valued in one finite subextension [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x]. Write $\mathcal C_E(T)=D^b_c(T,E)$ for the raw rationalization of derived-complete integral constructible complexes, with its specified completed finite scalar transitions $S_{F/E}$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Write $\mathcal C_T$ for the common-stage pair category of these $\mathcal C_E(T)$, with Hom groups the directed colimits over common finite fields [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. For $A=E_T,R_T$, let $\mathcal D_T(A)$ be the full subcategory of $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of bounded objects whose cohomology sheaves have a finite locally closed stratification on each stratum of which they are pro-etale locally finite free over $A$.

For each separated finite-type $k$-scheme $W$ use the rings, raw finite categories and common-stage categories defined above with $W$ replacing $T$. Let $J_{E,W}=E_W\otimes^L_{B_{E,W}}-$ and $\rho_W(E,K)=R_W\otimes^L_{E_W}J_{E,W}K$, with the actual completed finite scalar transitions and balanced comparison maps. Equip $\rho_W$ with the tensorator obtained from the quotient maps $\chi_{K,L}:K\otimes^L L\to K\widehat\otimes^L L$ and balanced scalar multiplication, and with the Hom map defined by transposing realized evaluation for every permitted pair [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

Let $g:T\xrightarrow{\sim}U$ be any scheme isomorphism between separated finite-type $k$-schemes; $g$ is not required to be a $k$-morphism. Use its specified integral derived pullback and its rational and common-stage passages [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and the coefficient identifications induced by reindexing $(V\to T)$ as $(V\to U)$ and by inverse image of the quotient projections. There is a natural isomorphism
$$b_g:\rho_Tg^*\xrightarrow{\sim}g^*\rho_U.$$
It is induced on the integral coefficient representatives by exact inverse-image reindexing and balanced tensor multiplication. It carries the actual completion quotient cocones (including the zero shifted-product component), total K-flat tensor maps, and finite scalar comparison maps to their corresponding maps over $T$. It respects the specified tensorator, coefficient unit and evaluation-transpose Hom maps. For every finite coefficient extension its mixed scalar square commutes. For an identity isomorphism $b_g$ is the identity under the specified identity pullbacks; for composable scheme isomorphisms its two routes coincide under the actual pullback composition maps. This includes the semilinear geometric Frobenius isomorphism when a finite-field descent datum is supplied, without a $k$-linearity assumption.

proof.text: Construct SpaceData at each space from the given R, P, A, N and H. The exact-derived section equivalence preserves full faithfulness and essential image. All realization, tensor and finite-normalization projections retain exactly the supplied data.
Apply normalized integral/common-stage reindexing to this objectwise family, obtaining FamilyCore with its original data and the ordinary section and integral normalization equations.

Use normalized functoriality for identity/composition, normalized tensor compatibility for tensor/unit, and the evaluation-transpose lemma for Hom. Assemble these fields with the unchanged FamilyCore into Family.
The equality of objectwise data gives all three required equalities by projection. The remaining mixed common-stage equation is naturality of comparison.hom on StageSystem.isoToStage.
